subject: Routing purchase: Marketplace vs Enterprise contract — billing, deployment, and co-sell implications
messages:
From: Ethan Reynolds <ethan.reynolds@finlytics.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 09:05:12 -0700
Subject: Marketplace vs enterprise contract — invoice timing and co-sell credits

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — FinLytics is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the private deployment option for our regulated workloads. Before we move to PO, procurement asked me to clarify two things so we can route the purchase correctly:

1) If we buy via AWS Marketplace (private offer or standard listing), how does invoicing work vs a direct enterprise contract (invoice from Redwood)? Specifically: PO acceptance timing, invoice receipt, and whether we can use our corporate card or have to do net-30.

2) For co-sell credits (we're working with an AWS ISV partner manager), what evidence or SKUs are required to qualify, and is there any delay to start receiving co-sell incentives if we go Marketplace vs direct?

Can you send a short comparison we can share with procurement and legal? A simple table (billing timing, tax handling, deployment options, contract terms, co-sell impact) would be ideal.

Thanks — we're aiming to decide by end of next week.

— Ethan
Ethan Reynolds

Ethan — great question and glad FinLytics liked the demo. Quick summary attached and below; I can also walk procurement/legal through details on a 30-min call.

High-level comparison (short):
- Marketplace (Private Offer): faster path to marketplace billing for AWS customers with PO acceptance via AWS; invoice routing through AWS Marketplace (can be net terms depending on your AWS setup). Sync to FinLytics finance depends on AWS invoice cycle (typically 30–45 days).
- Direct Enterprise (Redwood Invoice): Redwood issues invoice directly on our terms (we can offer net-30 or net-45 depending on contract). Faster clarity on billing cadence and easier to include non-standard payment terms.
- Co-sell: Marketplace listings make it straightforward for AWS partner managers to track usage/SKUs, but co-sell incentives often have lead times — partner team confirmation required. Direct deals can be registered with AWS partner team for co-sell but may need an MSA amendment for partner attribution.

I've attached a one-sheet matrix (Redwood_Marketplace_vs_Private_Offer_Table.xlsx) and a draft private-offer term sheet for procurement review. Proposed next step: 30-min call Tues or Wed to pick a routing.

Available times: Tue 9:00–11:00 PT, Wed 14:00–16:00 PT. Which works?

Cheers,

Quick answers so you can share with FinLytics today: 

Marketplace (Private Offer)
- Listing timeline: private offer creation + internal review ~ 1–2 weeks, marketplace sync to production billing ~ 4–6 additional weeks (so ~5–8 weeks end-to-end).
- Invoicing: AWS issues consolidated invoice to customer and remits to Redwood after their billing cycle; for enterprises that use AWS purchase orders, invoice reconciliation is on the AWS invoice (30–45 day lag typical).
- Pricing/discounts: Marketplace private offers typically include a negotiated discount to list price; expect to model ~10–20% depending on channel incentives. That discount reduces Redwood's net ASP; sales compensation and margin need to reflect that.
- Co-sell: AWS partner registration can be tied to a marketplace private offer, but co-sell incentives require partner manager approval and evidence (workorder, usage forecast, signed PO). Timing to receive credits depends on AWS pipeline entry; assume 1–2 quarters for realized incentives.

Direct Enterprise Invoice (Redwood Invoice)
- Listing timeline: N/A.
- Invoicing: Redwood invoices directly on agreed payment terms (net-30/net-45). This gives procurement immediate clarity on payment calendar and avoids AWS invoice lag.
- Pricing/discounts: We can provide bespoke pricing/commit terms without marketplace fee. Better for margin retention.
- Co-sell: We can register direct deals for co-sell, but the partner manager will still need deal evidence; attribution is possible but may require additional Partner Portal steps.

Legal / Compliance notes:
- For regulated FinTech: recommend adding data residency clause for private deployment and explicit audit logging SLA. Avoid broad indemnity language in the marketplace private offer — we can keep legal language consistent with our enterprise MSA.

Suggested reply to procurement: offer both routing options in parallel: finalize private offer terms for quick acceptance while we provision a direct Redwood invoice path if procurement prefers direct billing. Ask FinLytics which they prefer for cashflow (AWS billing lag vs Redwood invoice).

If helpful I can jump on the call with Mateo and FinLytics procurement to walk through the timeline.

— Laura Bennett

Ethan — thanks for the quick turn. Per our internal check (summary below) and the attached comparison, here are the recommended next steps so procurement has a clean path: 

1) Parallel approach (recommended):
   - We prepare a private offer on AWS (aiming to have it created within 1 week) so procurement can accept via AWS Private Offers. This preserves the co-sell friendliness of a marketplace route.
   - Simultaneously finalize a short Redwood invoice addendum (we can issue the first invoice on net-30) so your finance team can book and schedule payment immediately if they prefer direct billing.

2) Timelines: private offer listing end-to-end ~ 5–8 weeks for full billing sync; direct Redwood invoice provides immediate invoicing on signature.

3) Co-sell: we'll engage our partner manager and request co-sell registration concurrently; expect incentive realization later in the quarter. We will share the exact SKUs and evidence pack required this week.

Action items for FinLytics procurement: please confirm which path you prefer for invoicing (AWS invoice lag acceptable vs direct Redwood invoice) and pick a 30-min slot for a short call. If you want us to proceed with parallel tracks we will prepare the private offer draft and the Redwood invoice addendum and share both by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — looping in Laura and Karthik for any last-minute edits to terms.

Best,
